asr.full_text: all right welcome everyone my name is Katherine Guu and i'm the head of product for digital assets at solana foundation uh here with me today is TJ from FireBlockz, TJ how are you doing i'm doing great katherine great to be here yeah um you know like maybe we can pick up with just something about yourself your role at FireBlockz and what is fireblocks yep uh so uh at fireblocks uh I am leading our solutions engineering architecture team in the Americas. So we work with a lot of our enterprise customers using the Fireblox technology. So what is Fireblox? Fireblox is the global leader of digital asset infrastructure. Really our goal is to provide an easy-to-use, secure, scalable platform that empowers institutions to build on digital assets. So we're seeing that with everything from simple crypto trading use cases when we first got started to now more utility use cases like payments, stable coins, tokenized real world assets. And we've really built a platform that has been able to grow with this market and our customers and keeping them secure. Yeah that's awesome and I think many people on this kind of podcast know 5Blocks very well because you guys are being trusted by over 2,000 different financial institutions worldwide which is very impressive, so I guess, you know as we start to collaborate, in terms of building out the Solana Developer Platform and having Fireblocks as one of the very first design partners to really build this thing out for us what kind of capabilities that you would like to, kind of get being built out within STP? Yeah, so really excited to be involved with ST sdp um so you know solana is making it very easy uh through uh you know kind of an api first product through sdp to make building on solana very easy um so i think this has a lot of benefits to you know institutions just getting into digital assets uh But there's also some interesting possibilities there with, you know, the advent of A.I. agents. And, you know, they can just go and very quickly spin up, you know, an account on Solana developer platform and get building. So in terms of, you know, Fireblocks, where we kind of help out and fit, you know, we're providing a comprehensive set of wallet tools and services addressing the needs of Security, Custody, compliance, & Operational efficiency. When an institution wants to engage in digital assets at scale and securely, the five blocks really can come in & manage many complexities of that, while making sure that they stay secure. complexities of that while making sure that that business stays secured. So some of the specific things that we do there first and foremost it's enterprise wallet infrastructure, robust transaction workflows to actually operationalize these tokens and these products, compliance controls to make sure that these organizations are operating compliantly, asset custody transfer and settlement and you know utility in the greater Solana network right not just holding these tokens but actually using them you know whether or not it's defi or anything else right making sure that that connectivity is there. Awesome. And of course, with the recent acquisition of dynamic i think it makes things higher offering even richer right and we already have itai on the show as well to talk about what he envisions i guess like from your vantage point it might be helpful just to think about some specific um or popular enterprise use cases that you can think of which requires a combination of having both that custodial institutional grade experience as well as having that embedded wallace as well maybe walk us through maybe any example that come to your mind yeah so they're very complementary to each other uh they do uh you know uh fulfill different needs and use cases. So on the dynamic side, that's been a great acquisition for us. They are, you know, one of the easiest to use embedded wallets. So typically you would see those as, you know, I'm a platform like SDP and I want to make it easy to onboard users that may or may not have a wallet. And so, you know, we've seen that with a lot of exchanges, tokenisation platforms where they want to issue them a wallet, but they still want to sort of control and make that user experience wonderful, while maintaining self custody for the end user. On the Firebloc side, it's traditionally direct custody So, the institution needs to manage their treasury or it's an institution issuing a tokenized real-world asset. They need to own the Solana program, the minting rights, and the transfer rights to that they need to do that with the most secure wallet. And that's really where Fireblolood kind of comes in. So the nice thing about sort of the dynamic between the two no pun intended, is, you know, migrating from dynamic to a FireBlox wallet is relatively straightforward, and vice versa, because at the end of the day, these are normal Solana accounts, right? All of the security things that we're doing or at least the majority of the Security things that we're doing those are primarily being done to off chain and fire blocks. So if in the event, you know, somebody wants to start off and sell their Platform with like an embedded wallet dynamic. It's very easy for them to then transfer that ownership over to a Fireblocks wallet or maybe start, you know, do the do a fresh deployment from the Fireblocks wallet. And what that will give them is, you know, all those kind of extensive layers of defense and def, so that starts with zero-trust architecture and how Fireblocks is built, multi-device approvals, so making sure that you're not just using Ledger device it is, or, you know, you're not just using larger devices or, you know, specific hardware devices, you have multiple devices that you can use. We use distributed MPC wallet infrastructure. All of the secrets as part of our system leverage hardware security enclaves, so trust and execution environments for key materials, as well as other secrets. And then any sensitive action is enforced to a policy and governance engine, so that means, you know, there shouldn't be a single user, internal user within the organization that can do something malicious or nefarious. And, you know, the whole idea is to prevent some of the biggest hacks that we've seen recently where, you know, the on-chain protocol was fine, but ultimately, you know, the private keys of we've seen recently, where the on-chain protocol was fine, but ultimately, the private keys, the account was compromised, Fireblocks is built from the ground up to prevent those types of attacks. Yeah, I think, if anything, lessons learned is to that social engineering aspect, how we can avoid the human error and to use other tools to really minimize the effect. And I think that brings us to a nice point just to focus a little bit more on exactly what sort of policy engine is capable, like within the five blocks engine, because I think that's super critical. And my related question is also the same kind of rigor that is capable within the five blocks custodial setup. Can that also be like one-to-one, portable over to the dynamic side and having that embedded experience as well? Yep. They are different products built for different uses, right? So, dynamic is going to be more for, again, onboarding users simply and securely. The dynamic team does have some really strong policy controls there, but it's purpose-built more for let's say individual users, small teams, whereas FIRE BLOX is purpose-built for some of the largest institutions in the world. So think of some of the largest crypto trading companies. They use FIRE BLOX in their backend for custody, governance and policies to secure to make sure hey they can source the liquidity's they can source crypto for their users you know custody it for them outside of key management and MPC the biggest piece of that is is what you're referring to the policy and governance layers so that really starts with you know aand-death model and basically role-based access control. So there should be no user within the Fireblocks system that has unfettered access to do anything without another user approving it. to satisfy the user, right, because ultimately these are their internal controls that the FIreblock's solution is enforcing cryptographically on their behalf, right? So this is how we can, you know, prevent things like some of the Gnosis safe hacks that we've seen over the last couple of years, right? Where, you know, some of that logic is just on a smart contract but then you know the off-chain interface gets compromised uh and you know the user thinks they're signing something legitimate but they're you know actually sending all their funds to uh north korea yeah and i guess a follow-up question i'm more specific tied into the solana program here right and you and as we discussing some of our other design calls, it's like, how do we think about implementing Fireblocks policy engine to be complimentary and really to further strengthen a lot of the token extension features within SDP, which is what we're using right now across all of the issuance of different kinds of assets? Yep. So this is one of the reasons that I really love Solana and the token standards, token extensions and the native support that you have for that, let's say versus like other ecosystems where maybe you have to roll your own smart contract or, import a third party one and potential vulnerabilities with that. So FireBlock's plus Solana here is a very natural fit. Solana has handled all the on-chains who are role-based access control and security of the token—the token extensions that different roles within that. And then on FireBlock side, we're handling all the off-chain security of okay you know let's say you have you know five different Solana accounts within your token that need to do minting burning transferring you know updating metadata well those can now be mapped to five different firebox accounts which now off-chain have all this off-chain security that I was talking about. So, you know, all the policy, use governance, zero trust, all of those things. Yeah, fantastic. And you know, we're certainly very looking forward to working with you guys. I guess my last ending question is what excites you the most about Sovana? So, you know, the native token extensions is a great one that I just mentioned. But, you know, the growth is the other big one. Right. So we're seeing a ton of uptake on Solana for that exact reason. And you know, one of the things that we've seen here as infrastructure provider is with that growth, it's actually been you know. It's been a lot of fun to grow along. It's been challenging, right? This came up most, most notably, during the Trump and Malami Melania coin meme coin frenzy. So there was a huge rush, you know, first, you know, and its activity on Salana spiked. We saw 1000% increase on our customers interacting with Solana. And, you know, we were able to our customers interacting with CELANA. And we were able to grow in scale with that, right? So that was really exciting. And so, that was the meme coin phase. But now we're seeing a lot of tokenized real world assets. You know, I love the meme coins, that'll always be a good place in crypto, but it's nice to see some of the tokenized real world assets here as well. I'm so excited to to grow along with you all on that journey. Awesome. Well, thank you so much for your time, TJ, today. Would love keep working with you guys and definitely looking forward to more cool features getting pushed out from SDP together with you guys. Thanks, Catherine.
